openclaw/openclaw#68945.title: [Bug]: Telegram: humanDelay is not applied between streamed block replies

labels.name: regression
labels.description: Behavior that previously worked and now fails

openclaw/openclaw#68945.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

## Summary

`agents.defaults.humanDelay` (and per-agent `humanDelay` overrides) have no effect on the Telegram channel. Block replies produced by the Telegram streaming pipeline are sent back-to-back with no human-like pacing, even when `humanDelay.mode` is set to `natural` or `custom`.

Every other messaging channel wires `resolveHumanDelayConfig(cfg, agentId)` into its dispatcher; the Telegram extension does not.

## Version

- OpenClaw: `v2026.4.15` (also verified on `origin/main` at `c67a9c5259` and `v2026.4.19-beta.2`)
- Channel: Telegram (bot API, long polling)

### Steps to reproduce

## Config used

```json5
{
  agents: {
    defaults: {
      humanDelay: { mode: "custom", minMs: 800, maxMs: 2500 }
    }
  },
  channels: {
    telegram: {
      streaming: {
        mode: "block",
        block: {
          enabled: true,
          coalesce: { idleMs: 3000, maxChars: 200, minChars: 40 }
        },
        chunkMode: "newline"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Expected behavior

## Expected

When block streaming fires 3 coalesced messages, a randomized pause in `[minMs, maxMs]` should be inserted before every block after the first (the same behavior `reply-dispatcher.ts` already implements for other channels).

### Actual behavior

## Actual

All 3 messages arrive back-to-back (~500 ms apart, limited only by `coalesce.idleMs` / API latency). No humanDelay pause between them.

### OpenClaw version

2026.4.15

### Operating system

ubuntu

### Install method

npn global

### Model

claude-sonnet-4.6

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> anthropic api

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs, screenshots, and evidence

```shell

```

### Impact and severity

_No response_

### Additional information

## Root cause

`src/auto-reply/reply/reply-dispatcher.ts` applies `humanDelay` only when `ReplyDispatcherOptions.humanDelay` is supplied by the caller. Every channel passes it in via `resolveHumanDelayConfig(cfg, agentId)`:

- `extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/dispatch.ts:544`
- `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.ts:728`
- `extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.ts:305`
- `extensions/imessage/src/monitor/monitor-provider.ts:445`
- `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/handler.ts:1418`
- `extensions/msteams/src/reply-dispatcher.ts:255`
- `extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.ts:367`
- `extensions/tlon/src/monitor/index.ts:551`
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.ts:597` / `:1522`

Telegram does not:

- `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.ts:602` builds `dispatcherOptions` for `dispatchReplyWithBufferedBlockDispatcher` without a `humanDelay` field.
- No file under `extensions/telegram/src/` references `humanDelay` or `resolveHumanDelayConfig` (`git grep -l humanDelay extensions/telegram/` is empty on all refs).

## Suggested fix

Wire the same helper into the Telegram dispatch call:

```ts
// extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.ts near line 602
({ queuedFinal } = await telegramDeps.dispatchReplyWithBufferedBlockDispatcher({
  ctx: ctxPayload,
  cfg,
  dispatcherOptions: {
    ...replyPipeline,
    humanDelay: resolveHumanDelayConfig(cfg, route.agentId),
    deliver: async (payload, info) => { /* ... */ },
  },
}));
```

This mirrors the Slack/Discord/Signal integrations and should be enough to make the existing `HumanDelayConfig` flow through the Telegram block-streaming path.

## Related

- Closed-stale: #17446 *Per-channel humanDelay config + debounce jitter* — proposed `channels.<channel>.humanDelay` for exactly this use case; closed by the stale bot without implementation.
- Open, tangential: #14428 (per-agent override — already implemented), #10566 (proportional mode — separate feature).

## Minor doc-bug noted along the way

In `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-dispatcher.ts:35-38`, `minMs`/`maxMs` are read only when `mode === "custom"`; `mode: "natural"` silently ignores them and always uses the hardcoded 800/2500. Users naturally expect `{ mode: "natural", minMs: 150, maxMs: 2000 }` to respect the overrides. Either documenting the ignore more loudly or letting `natural` honor overrides would reduce confusion.

openclaw/openclaw#68944.title: CLI commands hang at WebSocket gateway handshake (OpenClaw 2026.4.15)
openclaw/openclaw#68944.body:
# CLI Commands Hang at WebSocket Gateway Handshake

## Bug Description

Every CLI subcommand that requires a live gateway connection hangs indefinitely. The CLI successfully connects to the gateway WebSocket endpoint and receives the `connect.challenge` nonce, but then never sends the `connect.reply` — the command hangs until killed.

Commands that bypass the gateway transport (`--version`, `--help`) work correctly.

## Environment

- OpenClaw: 2026.4.15 (041266a)
- Node: v24.13.1
- NPM: 11.10.1
- OS: Windows Server 2022 x64 (Windows_NT 10.0.20348)
- Platform: VPS-760407
- Gateway: Running as scheduled task under SYSTEM account
- Auth: token + device identity (`~/.openclaw/identity/`)

## Affected Commands

| Command | Result | Latency |
|---------|--------|---------|
| `openclaw --version` | ✅ OK | 375ms |
| `openclaw --help` | ✅ OK | 114ms |
| `openclaw sessions` | ❌ HANG | 8000ms+ |
| `openclaw cron list` | ❌ HANG | 8000ms+ |
| `openclaw status` | ❌ HANG | 8300ms+ |
| `openclaw doctor` | ❌ HANG | 8000ms+ |
| `openclaw channels list` | ❌ HANG | 8200ms+ |
| `openclaw models list` | ❌ HANG | 8200ms+ |
| `openclaw agents list` | ❌ HANG | 8200ms+ |
| `openclaw gateway status` | ❌ HANG | 8200ms+ |
| `openclaw backup list` | ❌ HANG | 6200ms+ |
| `openclaw tui` | ❌ HANG | 6200ms+ |

## Root Cause Tracing

Using a WebSocket client with the auth token to trace the connection flow:

1. CLI spawns node process → connects to `ws://localhost:18789/gateway` ✅
2. Gateway sends `connect.challenge` event with nonce ✅
3. CLI receives the challenge ✅
4. **CLI hangs** — never sends `connect.reply` with signed nonce ❌
5. Gateway waits indefinitely, command times out

The CLI receives the nonce but appears to fail silently when generating/sending the signed reply. This blocks the entire command.

## What Was Tried

1. **CLI reinstall** — `npm uninstall -g openclaw` + `npm install -g openclaw@2026.4.15`
   - Result: Same behavior, issue persists
2. **Gateway restart** via scheduled task (`Stop-ScheduledTask` + `Start-ScheduledTask`)
   - Result: Same behavior after restart
3. **WebSocket trace** using `ws` library with HMAC-SHA256 signed nonce
   - Result: Gateway rejects HMAC-signed connections, confirming the CLI should use device keypair (EC P-256) signing

## Device Identity Status

- `identity/device.json` — intact, valid EC keypair
- `identity/device-auth.json` — intact, operator token with correct scopes
- Device ID: `20512fa1c7948b21355756331b40ee88c8e3d27b033ca619b2620d4995cb48f`

## Possible Causes

1. **Node.js v24.x crypto change** — v24.13.1 may have changed behavior in `crypto.sign()` / `crypto.verify()` for EC P-256 keys
2. **CLI device signing silently fails** — the signing code path returns an error that is swallowed, causing the CLI to never send the reply
3. **CLI respawn transport issue** — the CLI respawns itself with modified `NODE_OPTIONS`; the respawned process may have a different crypto state
4. **Stale nonce rejection** — gateway may be rejecting nonces from the current CLI process as replayed or malformed

## Logs

```
# CLI trace output
Connecting to ws://localhost:18789/gateway with token...
OPEN
Received: {"type":"event","event":"connect.challenge","payload":{"nonce":"b5e9bb7c-acc1-4d0f-957e-f29b3964e112","ts":1776586770161}}
Got nonce: b5e9bb7c-acc1-4d0f-957e-f29b3964e112
Signing with HMAC-SHA256...
Sent reply
[5s timeout] — never receives connect.ack
```

```
# Gateway log (last entry before CLI test)
2026-04-09T12:34:09.320+02:00 [gateway] log file: \tmp\openclaw\openclaw-2026-04-09.log
2026-04-09T12:34:09.327+02:00 [gateway] starting channels and sidecars...
2026-04-09T12:34:11.255+02:00 [hooks] loaded 4 internal hook handlers
2026-04-09T12:34:11.264+02:00 [plugins] embedded acpx runtime backend registered
2026-04-09T12:34:11.346+02:00 [browser] control listening on http://127.0.0.1:18791/
2026-04-09T12:34:16.681+02:00 [plugins] embedded acpx runtime backend ready
```

Gateway log does not show the CLI connection attempt — the challenge is sent but no corresponding connection is logged as established.

## Impact

- All CLI subcommands that interact with the gateway are unusable
- Cannot inspect sessions, cron jobs, channel status, model configs
- Automated scripts that rely on CLI fail
- Gateway health (HTTP) is fine — only the WebSocket transport is affected
- Rubble Board and direct file reads continue to work as a workaround

## Workaround

- Direct file reads of JSON state files (sessions, cron configs) work in milliseconds
- Gateway HTTP endpoints respond correctly (`/health` in 6ms)
- Rubble Board provides a web UI that bypasses the broken CLI transport

## Suggestion

1. Add logging to the CLI's challenge reply generation — the signing failure is currently silent
2. Add a timeout on the gateway side for pending challenges — this prevents a stuck CLI from holding resources indefinitely
3. Consider HMAC fallback if device key signing fails — the gateway currently rejects HMAC nonces, making debugging harder
4. Add CLI-level tracing for the WS handshake: `openclaw --log-level trace sessions` to expose where exactly it hangs

openclaw/openclaw#68931.title: [Bug]: Webchat user messages disappear due to race condition between chat history reload and transcript persistence
openclaw/openclaw#68931.body:
## Bug Description

User messages can disappear from the OpenClaw webchat UI after being sent. The message is typed, sent, briefly appears, then vanishes. The user did not delete it — the message disappears on its own.

## Root Cause Analysis

After analyzing the webchat frontend code and gateway logs, I identified a **race condition** between the chat history reload function and the transcript persistence:

### Message Flow
1. User types and sends a message
2. UI immediately adds the user message to `chatMessages` locally and sets `chatSending = true`
3. UI sends `chat.send` via WebSocket to the gateway
4. Gateway responds quickly with `{ runId, status: "started" }`
5. Gateway **asynchronously** persists the user message to the session transcript via `emitUserTranscriptUpdate()` — this is non-blocking
6. Gateway broadcasts a `session.message` event to connected clients
7. UI receives the event and calls `up()` — the chat history loader

### The Race Condition
The `up()` function **completely replaces** the local `chatMessages` array with whatever the server returns:

```js
e.chatMessages = (Array.isArray(i.messages) ? i.messages : []).filter(...)
```

If `up()` is called **before** the gateway has finished writing the user message to the transcript, the server returns a history that does NOT include the just-sent message. The local copy (which had the message) is overwritten with the server version (which does not), and the message disappears from the UI.

### When This Happens

The race is most likely to occur when:

1. **Model API errors/timeout** — When the model provider fails (e.g. `terminated`, timeout), error events can trigger a history reload before the transcript is fully written. Gateway logs confirmed a `terminated` error on the same run where the message disappeared.
2. **WebSocket reconnect** — After a disconnect/reconnect cycle, the UI reloads chat history from the server, losing any locally-added but not-yet-persisted messages.
3. **`up()` called from multiple event handlers** — The function is called from at least 6 different places (session change, session.message event, reconnect, /new, /reset, agent change, refresh), any of which can trigger the overwrite.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the webchat UI in a browser
2. Send a message while the model provider is slow or intermittently failing
3. Observe: the message appears briefly in the chat
4. Observe: the message disappears when the UI reloads chat history
5. The message may or may not appear in the session transcript on the server

## Expected Behavior

- User messages should **never disappear** once displayed in the UI
- The `up()` function should **merge** server history with local messages rather than replacing the entire array
- Or: the gateway should **await** the transcript persistence before broadcasting events that trigger history reloads

## Suggested Fixes

### Fix 1: Merge instead of replace in `up()`
When loading chat history from the server, preserve locally-added messages that are not yet in the server response. Match by message content + timestamp to avoid duplicates.

### Fix 2: Await transcript persistence before broadcasting
In the gateway `chat.send` handler, `await emitUserTranscriptUpdate()` before broadcasting the `session.message` event that triggers the UI reload. This ensures the server always has the message before the UI asks for it.

### Fix 3: Optimistic UI with reconciliation
Keep the local message in `chatMessages` with a pending flag. When `up()` returns server history, reconcile by replacing the pending message with the persisted version (matching by runId or content). If the server version does not include it yet, keep the local version.

## Environment

- OpenClaw gateway running on macOS (Mac Mini M4)
- Webchat via browser (control-ui)
- Model: nvidia/z-ai/glm-5.1 (NVIDIA API integration)
- Gateway logs confirmed: `embedded_run_agent_end` with `error: "terminated"` on the same run where the message disappeared

## Related

- #68811 — Feature request for real-time console/activity stream in webchat (which would also help users see that their message is being processed, reducing confusion when the UI appears frozen)

openclaw/openclaw#68921.title: Browser plugin: _snapshotForAI missing against Playwright 1.53+ (ariaSnapshot); 'Restart the gateway' error is misleading for dep mismatches
openclaw/openclaw#68921.body:
## What happens

The browser plugin's AI-snapshot code path (`dist/pw-ai-*.js`) calls `page._snapshotForAI(...)` against the `playwright-core` Page instance. That method is an **internal** API that Playwright deprecated/renamed in 1.53 and removed by 1.59; it is now the public `ariaSnapshot()`. Return shape also changed — old returned `{full: string}`, new returns a bare `string`.

Installing openclaw in an environment where `playwright-core` resolves to ≥ 1.53 (my install has 1.59.1, bundled via openclaw's own `node_modules/playwright-core`) means every `refs=aria` tool call throws at the guard:

```
Error: refs=aria requires Playwright _snapshotForAI support.
```

before the request ever reaches Chrome. CDP, Chrome itself, and the browser control service are all healthy; the problem is purely in the plugin's JS.

## Why it looks like "the bridge keeps falling"

`session-tab-registry-*.js` wraps Playwright timeouts (and any error containing `timed out|timeout|aborted`) with `BROWSER_TOOL_MODEL_HINT`:

> "Do NOT retry the browser tool — it will keep failing. Use an alternative approach or inform the user that the browser is currently unavailable. Restart the OpenClaw gateway."

In a dependency-mismatch scenario, the recommended restart **cannot fix it**. The agent restarts, the plugin comes back, the same missing method throws again on the next snapshot call. Users experience this as "the bridge keeps falling," and the suggested recovery action is actively wrong — restarts just replay the same failure.

## Where the calls are

In the minified `dist/pw-ai-*.js` (hashed filename, currently `pw-ai-BJRFEth4.js`), two call sites:

```js
// site 1 — generic snapshot
const maybe = page;
if (!maybe._snapshotForAI) throw new Error("Playwright _snapshotForAI is not available. Upgrade playwright-core.");
let snapshot = (await maybe._snapshotForAI({
    timeout: Math.max(500, Math.min(6e4, Math.floor(opts.timeoutMs ?? 5e3))),
    track: "response"
}))?.full ?? "";

// site 2 — refs=aria mode
if (!maybe._snapshotForAI) throw new Error("refs=aria requires Playwright _snapshotForAI support.");
const built = buildRoleSnapshotFromAiSnapshot((await maybe._snapshotForAI({
    timeout: 5e3,
    track: "response"
}))?.full ?? "", opts.options);
```

## Suggested fix

Prefer `ariaSnapshot` when present, fall back to `_snapshotForAI` for older Playwright. Diff shape for each site:

```diff
-  if (!maybe._snapshotForAI) throw new Error("...");
-  (await maybe._snapshotForAI({timeout, track: "response"}))?.full
+  if (!maybe.ariaSnapshot && !maybe._snapshotForAI) throw new Error("...");
+  (maybe.ariaSnapshot
+    ? (await maybe.ariaSnapshot({timeout, _track: "response"}))
+    : (await maybe._snapshotForAI({timeout, track: "response"}))?.full)
```

Note: `ariaSnapshot` accepts `_track` (underscore) as the track arg in 1.59.1, and `Locator.ariaSnapshot()` is already used elsewhere in the same file (the selector-scoped path at line ~1129 is fine — it's Page-level that's broken).

## Secondary: improve the error-hint wrapper

`BROWSER_TOOL_MODEL_HINT` / `resolveBrowserFetchOperatorHint` wraps Playwright timeouts with "Restart the OpenClaw gateway." For actual control-service unreachability this is correct, but for in-process Playwright errors (stale pages, missing prototype methods, locator timeouts from detached frames) it teaches the agent to attempt a recovery that never helps. Consider distinguishing **transport** failures from **operation** failures so only the former get the "restart gateway" hint.

## Environment

- openclaw 2026.4.15
- playwright-core 1.59.1 (resolved from `node_modules/playwright-core` under the global openclaw install)
- Node 22.x
- Linux / systemd user service

## Workaround in place

Until this ships I'm running a ~40-line Node `--require` shim via a systemd drop-in that adds a backward-compat `_snapshotForAI` to `Page.prototype` delegating to `ariaSnapshot`. Fine for a workaround, but ideally the plugin itself no longer depends on a renamed internal.

Happy to PR the two-site fix if it'd be useful — want to check whether you'd prefer the `ariaSnapshot`-preferred branch I sketched above or a cleaner "use only new API + bump playwright-core peerDep floor" approach.

openclaw/openclaw#68950.title: OAuth users cannot enable memory-lancedb auto-recall/capture without separate OPENAI_API_KEY
openclaw/openclaw#68950.body:
## Summary
Users authenticated to OpenClaw via OAuth/provider login still cannot enable the built-in `memory-lancedb` plugin unless they separately provide `OPENAI_API_KEY` for embeddings. This blocks the closest built-in equivalent to always-on active memory for users who intentionally rely on OAuth-only auth instead of raw API keys.

## Observed behavior
- `memory-lancedb` exists and advertises auto-recall/capture.
- Configuring it with embedding model + autoRecall/autoCapture is accepted structurally.
- Runtime/config then warns:
  - `plugins.entries.memory-lancedb.config.embedding.apiKey: Missing env var "OPENAI_API_KEY"`
- Plugin remains unavailable to OAuth-only users.
- `memory-core` remains the only practical path, but it does not provide the same auto-recall/capture behavior.

## Why this matters
- OAuth users should not be forced to add a separate OpenAI API key just to use built-in long-term memory auto-recall.
- It blocks a major memory feature for users who already authenticate through OpenClaw-supported provider login.

## Expected behavior
One of:
1. allow `memory-lancedb` embeddings to use the already authenticated provider session,
2. support provider-routed embeddings without requiring raw `OPENAI_API_KEY`,
3. document a supported OAuth-compatible path for auto-recall/capture memory.

## Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.4.15
- macOS
- agent using OAuth-authenticated provider session

## Summary
Running `rem-backfill` for a non-main agent can write dream output into the wrong workspace.

## Repro
Command run:
```bash
openclaw memory rem-backfill --agent stack --path /Users/boazooz/.openclaw/stack-workspace/memory --stage-short-term
```

## Observed behavior
CLI output reported:
- `workspace=~/.openclaw/workspace`
- `sourcePath=~/.openclaw/stack-workspace/memory`
- `dreamsPath=~/.openclaw/workspace/DREAMS.md`

So the source path was Stack's workspace, but the dream output path was the main workspace.

This creates cross-agent contamination risk.

## Why this matters
- REM/dream backfill should be agent-local.
- Writing dream outputs for one agent into another agent's workspace is unsafe and breaks memory isolation.

## Expected behavior
- `--agent stack` should resolve workspace artifacts to `~/.openclaw/stack-workspace`
- `dreamsPath` should be inside the stack workspace, not the main workspace
- short-term dream staging should also be agent-local

## Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.4.15
- macOS
- `stack` agent workspace: `/Users/boazooz/.openclaw/stack-workspace`

openclaw/openclaw#68946.title: Bug: Agent loops on identical tool calls without stopping
openclaw/openclaw#68946.body:
---
name: Tool Call Repetition Bug - Agent loops on identical tool calls
about: Agent repeatedly executes the same tool call (e.g., Get-ChildItem) 100+ times without stopping, even after receiving identical results.
title: "Bug: Agent loops on identical tool calls without stopping"
labels: ["bug", "agent-behavior", "high-priority"]
assignees: []
---

## Bug Description

The agent repeatedly executes the same tool call (e.g., `Get-ChildItem`, `curl`, `Invoke-RestMethod`) 100+ times in a single session, even after receiving identical results. This happens with static data queries (directory listings, file searches, API calls with no state changes).

**Impact:** Wasted tokens, slow response, poor user experience.

**Frequency:** High - happens consistently with the same pattern.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Agent receives a task involving static data query (e.g., "check D:\OpenClaw-Agents directory structure")
2. Agent executes tool call (e.g., `Get-ChildItem`)
3. Agent receives result
4. Agent does NOT check if result is identical to previous call
5. Agent executes SAME tool call again
6. Steps 3-5 repeat until session limit or timeout

**Example from 2026-04-19:**
- 9:07-11:04: 100+ repeated `Get-ChildItem` calls
- 12:44-13:33: 50+ repeated file search calls
- 13:47: 20+ repeated message sends

## Root Cause Analysis

### Why it happens (from agent's self-reflection):

1. **Memory files are "passive"** - MEMORY.md is only read once at session startup, not checked before each tool call
2. **No "operation dedup"** - Agent doesn't check "have I done this before?" before generating tool call
3. **No "result comparison"** - Agent doesn't automatically compare "is this result same as last time?"
4. **No hard limit in system prompt** - System prompt has no constraint like "same operation max N times"

### What agent wrote:

> "记忆文件是'被动读取'，不是'自动执行的规则'
> 我没有在每次生成 tool call 前检查'这个操作是否已经做过'
> 系统提示到来时，我机械地重新生成命令，而不是先判断'是否需要新的操作'"

## Proposed Solutions

### Solution 1: System-level tool call dedup (P0)

**What:** Add automatic deduplication at the system level, not relying on agent self-restraint.

**How:**
- Before executing any tool call, system checks if same tool+params executed within last N calls
- If identical result detected, system forces agent to stop and analyze
- Hard limit: max 3 executions per operation type per session

**Benefits:**
- Doesn't rely on agent self-awareness
- Works even if agent "forgets" or "doesn't notice"
- Catches loops that agent misses

### Solution 2: Result comparison mechanism (P0)

**What:** System automatically compares consecutive tool call results.

**How:**
- After each tool call, system hashes/compares result with previous result
- If 100% identical, system warns agent: "Result identical to previous call. Stop and analyze."
- If 3+ identical results, system forces stop

**Benefits:**
- Automatic detection, no manual checking
- Works for all tool types (exec, read, write, etc.)
- Reduces false positives (allows legitimate repeated calls with different params)

### Solution 3: Operation counter (P1)

**What:** Track operation counts per type.

**How:**
- System maintains counter per operation type (e.g., Get-ChildItem: 0, curl: 0)
- Each execution increments counter
- If counter > 3 for same operation, system warns agent
- If counter > 5, system forces stop

**Benefits:**
- Prevents "query → query → query" loops
- Works even if results vary slightly
- Simple to implement

### Solution 4: Session-level limits (P1)

**What:** Hard limits on total tool calls per session.

**How:**
- Max 50 tool calls per session (configurable)
- If limit reached, system forces agent to summarize and stop
- Agent must prioritize: which calls are most important?

**Benefits:**
- Prevents runaway sessions
- Forces agent to be efficient
- Reduces token waste

## Implementation Priority

| Priority | Solution | Effort | Impact |
|----------|----------|--------|--------|
| P0 | Tool call dedup | Medium | High |
| P0 | Result comparison | Medium | High |
| P1 | Operation counter | Low | Medium |
| P1 | Session limits | Low | Medium |

## Workaround (Current)

Agent self-restraint rules (not reliable):
- MEMORY.md contains "tool call stop rule"
- Agent manually checks before each tool call
- Works ~30% of the time (agent still loops 70% of time)

**Conclusion:** Self-restraint is not enough. Need system-level enforcement.

## Additional Context

- Happens most with static data queries (file listings, directory searches)
- Less common with state-changing operations (write, delete)
- Agent "knows" the rule but can't enforce it consistently
- This is a fundamental gap in agent architecture: no "stop condition" detection

## References

- Agent self-reflection: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/XXX (link to agent's own analysis)
- Similar bug reports: N/A (first reported)

## Next Steps

openclaw/openclaw#68955.title: [Feature]: Slash commands like /new should trigger ack reaction and typing indicator
openclaw/openclaw#68955.body:
### Summary ## Summary When using the Telegram channel with `reactionLevel: ack` + `ackReactionScope: direct`, regular messages correctly trigger the 👀 ack reaction and typing indicator. However, slash commands like `/new` do not trigger these UX feedback mechanisms, leading to inconsistent user experience. ## Environment - OpenClaw: 2026.4.15 - Platform: macOS (Apple Silicon, M4 Pro) - Channel: Telegram (DM) - Installation: pnpm global ## Config ```json { "agents": { "defaults": { "typingMode": "instant", "typingIntervalSeconds": 6 } }, "channels": { "telegram": { "reactionLevel": "ack" } }, "messages": { "ackReactionScope": "direct" } } ``` ## Current behavior | Scenario | Behavior | |---|---| | Regular message in existing session | ✅ 👀 reaction + typing indicator appear instantly | | `/new` command | ❌ No reaction, no typing indicator | | Message sent immediately after `/new` | ⚠️ Reaction appears delayed, bundled with reply | ## Expected behavior Slash commands like `/new`, `/reset`, etc. should go through the same inbound message pipeline (or at least emit the same UX signals) as regular messages, so users see consistent feedback. ## Root cause (from investigation) Based on source code inspection, slash commands appear to be routed to a dedicated command handler that bypasses the normal inbound message pipeline where ack reactions and typing indicators are dispatched. The `/new` handler sends the greeting message directly without emitting these UX signals. ## Impact Low functional impact (the bot still works), but confusing UX: users sending `/new` see nothing happen until the greeting arrives, while the same bot is highly responsive to regular messages. In slower setups (e.g., local LLM with multi-second initialization), this gap is particularly noticeable. ## Suggested fix Either: 1. Route slash commands through the same pipeline that triggers ack/typing (simplest), or 2. Add explicit `sendAck()` / `startTyping()` calls at the start of slash command handlers. ## Related - `reactionLevel`, `ackReactionScope` config documented at [typing-indicators.md](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/typing-indicators) (if this path is correct — please correct) --- Happy to provide more logs or details if helpful. ### Problem to solve Problem to solveUsers relying on visual feedback (typing indicator, ack reaction emoji 👀) to confirm their message was received are left without any signal when they send a slash command like /new. Since slash commands are the natural way to manage sessions — users typing /new are explicitly starting a new conversation — the complete absence of feedback at this exact moment creates several real pain points:1. Indistinguishable from a broken botOn self-hosted setups with local LLMs, where initialization can take anywhere from a few seconds to over a minute (large model loading, MCP server warmup, session memory hooks), users have no way to tell whether: The bot received the command and is initializing a new session The bot is down or the gateway crashed The command itself was typed incorrectly The contrast is sharp: regular messages show 👀 instantly, proving the pipeline works. Users then assume /new not reacting means something is wrong, and often retry the command — spawning duplicate sessions or triggering race conditions.2. Inconsistent UX breaks user mental modelOnce users learn "OpenClaw always shows 👀 when it receives my message," the absence of 👀 on slash commands feels like a regression or bug. The official docs for typing-indicators describe instant mode as firing "as soon as the model loop begins" with no carve-out for commands, reinforcing the expectation that all inbound messages produce feedback.3. No graceful cue for long session resets/new can trigger non-trivial work under the hood (closing the old session, initializing memory context, running session-start hooks). For some setups this takes meaningful time, but the user sees a silent interface until the greeting finally arrives. A 👀 or typing indicator during this gap would communicate "working on it" just as it does for tool-heavy LLM responses.4. Workarounds are uglyThe only way users currently get feedback on session reset is to send /new followed immediately by a dummy message like "hi" — because the latter triggers the normal pipeline. This is awkward and defeats the purpose of having a clean slash command.Why current behavior is insufficientThe current architecture routes slash commands through a dedicated command handler that bypasses the normal inbound message pipeline where ack reactions and typing indicators are dispatched. This is likely an implementation choice (commands are synchronous and return quickly in most cases), but it assumes commands always complete fast enough that feedback is unnecessary — an assumption that breaks for: Local LLM deployments with cold start Slash commands that do real work (/new, /reset, custom /commands) Users coming from typical messenger UX where every message produces some form of receipt A minimal fix (emit ack reaction on command receipt, before delegating to the command handler) preserves the existing command handler architecture while closing the UX gap. ### Proposed solution

Proposed solution

Emit the ack reaction and (optionally) typing indicator for slash commands using the same mechanism as regular inbound messages, while keeping the existing dedicated command handler architecture intact.

Desired behavior

User sends /new
  ↓ (within ~100ms)
👀 reaction appears on user's /new message
  ↓ (if command takes >1s)
Typing indicator starts
  ↓ (when greeting is ready)
Bot sends greeting, 👍 reaction replaces 👀

This matches exactly what users already see for regular messages and preserves the existing reaction lifecycle (👀 → 🤔 → 🔥 → 👍, with 🥱/😨 for slow runs, 😱 for errors).

Minimal implementation sketch

At the top of the Telegram inbound dispatcher, before the slash-command vs. message branching, invoke the same ack/typing hooks currently used in the regular message path. Concretely:

js
// Pseudocode — actual paths depend on reply-*.js / pi-embedded-*.js chunks
async function handleInboundMessage(ctx) {
  // NEW: emit ack immediately, before routing decision
  if (shouldEmitAck(ctx)) {
    await emitAckReaction(ctx);       // 👀
    startTypingController(ctx);        // stored for lifecycle cleanup
  }

  if (isSlashCommand(ctx.message.text)) {
    return handleSlashCommand(ctx);    // existing handler
  }
  return handleRegularMessage(ctx);    // existing handler
}

Both handlers then share the same cleanup path (markRunComplete → 👍 on success, 😱 on error) that already exists for regular messages.

Configuration (backward compatible)

Add an optional per-channel flag to control this, defaulting to true so existing users benefit automatically:

json
{
  "channels": {
    "telegram": {
      "reactionLevel": "ack",
      "ackOnSlashCommands": true        // NEW, default: true
    }
  },
  "messages": {
    "ackReactionScope": "direct"
  }
}

Users who explicitly want the current silent behavior for commands can set ackOnSlashCommands: false.

Edge cases

Case | Proposed handling -- | -- Command completes in <200ms | Ack 👀 then 👍 fires normally. Typing never starts (below threshold). Command returns immediate error | 👀 → 😱 (same as regular messages). Built-in commands with no reply (e.g., /mute) | Emit 👀 → 👍 anyway so user sees receipt. Unknown/malformed command | Emit 👀 → 😱 or 🤷 (pick one). Currently silent — anything is better. High-frequency command spam | Same rate limits and TTL (typingTtlMs) as regular messages apply automatically.

Alternative (simpler) approach

If threading ack/typing through the command handler is too invasive, a one-line fix works: emit a single ack 👀 at command receipt, without typing and without the progression reactions. This alone eliminates the "is the bot even alive?" pain, even if commands that run long still feel silent after the initial 👀. Acceptable minimum viable fix.

What this explicitly does NOT change

  • No change to the command handler's business logic or return contract.
  • No change to regular message flow (already working).
  • No new permissions or Bot API scopes needed (Telegram's setMessageReaction already works for any message the bot can see in a DM).
  • No change to typingMode semantics — this is strictly about extending the existing ack/typing plumbing to slash commands.

Acceptance criteria

  1. Sending /new in a DM with reactionLevel: ack + ackReactionScope: direct produces 👀 within ~500ms, even on local LLM deployments where session init takes several seconds.
  2. /new in a DM produces typing indicator if the command takes longer than typingIntervalSeconds.
  3. On completion, 👀 is replaced by the same terminal reaction as regular messages (👍 success, 😱 error).
  4. Existing behavior for users with reactionLevel: off or ackReactionScope: group-mentions is unchanged.
  5. Rate limit and stuck-indicator safeguards (TTL, cleanup on error) apply identically to commands and regular messages — no new orphaned typing loops introduced.

Out of scope

  • Custom per-command reaction overrides (e.g., different emoji for /mute vs /new). Can be a follow-up issue.
  • Exposing command-start/end as hook points for plugins. Separate concern.
### Alternatives considered _No response_ ### Impact Impact Affected users/systems/channels Primary: Telegram channel users who have reactionLevel: ack (or more verbose) with ackReactionScope: direct configured. This is the recommended config for DM-heavy personal assistant setups per the existing reactionLevel documentation. Secondary (likely, not verified): Other channels with similar slash-command routing — Discord, Slack — if they share the same inbound dispatcher architecture. The root cause (commands bypass the message pipeline that emits ack/typing) is channel-agnostic, so the fix probably benefits them too. Most acutely affected: Self-hosted deployments using local LLMs (Ollama, MLX, llama.cpp) where /new triggers real work — new session init, KV cache miss, MCP server handshake, bootstrap system prompt assembly (often 10-30k tokens). In these setups, /new can take 30 seconds to 3+ minutes of silence before the greeting arrives. Least affected: Cloud-hosted setups with fast APIs (Anthropic, OpenAI) where /new completes in well under a second, so the silent gap is imperceptible. For these users the issue exists but is barely noticeable. Severity Confusing / erodes trust in the bot, but does not block workflow. The bot still works — users eventually get their greeting. But the silent gap during /new directly contradicts the instant feedback users see for every other message they send, which: Makes the bot feel broken or unresponsive at exactly the moment users are trying to re-engage it Undermines the value proposition of reactionLevel: ack itself — users enable it specifically to know the bot received their message, and it silently fails on the one command where confirmation matters most (a deliberate session reset) Creates a worse experience than having no feedback at all would, because the inconsistency itself is the problem — users learn "OpenClaw shows 👀 when it gets my message," then /new violates that learned model Not a P0/P1, but a real papercut that compounds with other latency issues (see frequency below). Frequency Always reproducible for any user with reactionLevel: ack + ackReactionScope: direct sending /new in Telegram DM. 100% of the time, no feedback appears on the /new message itself. How often the pain is felt: depends on usage pattern. Power users who start fresh sessions frequently (to avoid context bloat or switch topics) hit this multiple times per day. Casual users with long-running sessions hit it rarely. Intermittent severity: worse on local LLM setups with cold-start penalties. On a warm local model it's a 5-second gap; on a cold model with large MCP tool schemas it can be 2-3 minutes of silence. The same bug feels like a minor annoyance or a hard failure depending on deployment. Stacks with other issues: users already dealing with slow cold starts (unavoidable for local LLMs) have the added insult of no visual feedback. If one of these was fixed, the other would sting less. Consequence Retry spam: Users assume /new was lost and send it again. In my own setup I caught myself doing this within the first day of testing. Repeated /new in quick succession may create race conditions in session management (not verified), and at minimum wastes gateway cycles. Reduced trust in reaction UX overall: Once users learn "reactions are unreliable on commands," they start to ignore them generally, defeating the whole point of enabling reactionLevel. Workaround fatigue: The practical fix users discover is "send /new then immediately send a dummy message like hi," which is awkward, polluted session history with junk messages, and defeats the clean intent of slash commands. Manual troubleshooting tax: Anyone investigating "why is my Telegram bot not responding?" for /new specifically will end up digging through reactionLevel, ackReactionScope, Bot permissions, and ultimately OpenClaw source before discovering that slash commands simply aren't in the pipeline. This happened in my debugging session — roughly 45 minutes of investigation traced back to this architectural split. Future users will re-do this same investigation. Documentation drift risk: The typing-indicators docs describe typingMode: instant as firing "as soon as the model loop begins," which users reasonably interpret to include commands. Leaving the current behavior in place means either (a) updating the docs to carve out commands, adding complexity to the mental model, or (b) fixing the bug. (b) is cheaper long-term. Community support load: Search hits on GitHub issues and forums for "Telegram /new silent" or "reaction not appearing on command" will grow over time as more users adopt reactionLevel: ack. Fixing this proactively avoids a support backlog. Not impact To be honest about what this isn't: No data loss No security issue No regression — this behavior has likely existed since slash commands were introduced Bot functionality is fully preserved; the command executes correctly, just silently So this is a polish-level issue, but polish matters for a product whose selling point ("personal AI assistant with typing indicators and reaction emoji for natural conversational UX") depends on that polish being consistent across interactions. ### Evidence/examples _No response_ ### Additional information _No response_

openclaw/openclaw#67277.title: fix(context-window): Tighten context limits and bound memory excerpts
openclaw/openclaw#67277.body:
## What this PR is doing

This is a broad "make context loading less wasteful by default, without removing capability" pass.

The core idea is:

```ts
before:
  a bunch of context-heavy surfaces had generous defaults
  some reads were larger / less explicit than they needed to be
  memory_get could behave more like "read a lot from this file"
  tool-result truncation had a couple of inconsistent paths

after:
  high-volume surfaces are bounded more aggressively by default
  memory_get is a bounded exact-excerpt fetch with explicit partial-read signaling
  agents can override the new caps per agent
  live + persisted tool-result truncation are more internally consistent
```

## The main pieces

### 1. Lower default budgets for expensive context surfaces

This PR tightens several prompt/tool surfaces that quietly bloat context:

- bootstrap defaults are lower
- read-style file loading is tighter
- live tool-result caps are lower
- startup and post-compaction AGENTS injection is smaller
- memory qmd snippet/injection defaults are lower
- a few other web/media/browser surfaces are lower too

The point is not one magic knob. The point is reducing unnecessary context load across the main high-volume entry points.

### 2. `memory_get` becomes a bounded exact-excerpt fetch

`memory_get` stays source-file backed. It does **not** switch to returning index snippets.

But its contract is now more explicit and more bounded:

```ts
memory_get(path, from?, lines?)
```

Behavior now:

- omitted `from` starts at line 1
- omitted `lines` means a bounded default window, not "rest of file"
- result is capped by default max chars
- result tells the model when it got only part of the excerpt

Successful reads now return structured continuation state, not just bare text:

```ts
{
  path,
  text,
  truncated,
  from,
  lines,
  nextFrom
}
```

And when partial, the text also includes a short deterministic continuation notice so the model reliably knows to continue with `from=<nextFrom>`.

This behavior is mirrored across both memory host paths so builtin and packaged behavior stay aligned.

### 3. Add per-agent context limit overrides

This PR adds a focused config surface for runtime-owned bounded excerpts and injected prompt blocks:

```ts
agents.defaults.contextLimits
agents.list[].contextLimits
```

The main fields are:

```ts
memoryGetMaxChars
memoryGetDefaultLines
toolResultMaxChars
postCompactionMaxChars
```

So the new defaults are not hardcoded globally forever. They are now tunable per agent.

### 4. Fix two real tool-result truncation issues

This PR also fixes two concrete correctness gaps discovered during review:

- tool results were previously capped, then passed through persistence hooks, and hooks could expand them again before append
- persisted-session aggregate recovery still had an older floor that could weaken tiny explicit caps

The fixes make the truncation story more honest:

```ts
cap -> hook mutates -> cap again -> append
```

and ensure tiny configured caps are honored more consistently during recovery as well as normal live writes.

### 5. Keep skills budgeting separate from generic runtime excerpt budgeting

This PR does **not** route skills prompt sizing through the new generic `contextLimits` surface.

Instead the ownership remains split:

```ts
skills prompt budget != memory/tool-result/runtime excerpt budgets
```

That keeps the config model cleaner:

- skills prompt size stays under `skills.limits` / `agents.list[].skillsLimits`
- runtime bounded excerpt/injection size lives under `contextLimits`

### 6. Update docs so the ownership model is understandable

The docs now describe the budget ownership map more explicitly:

- bootstrap limits
- startupContext limits
- skills prompt limits
- agents.defaults.contextLimits.*
- memory.qmd limits

That matters because before this, it was too easy to assume these were all controlled by one knob when they were not.

## What this PR intentionally does not do

This PR does **not** try to solve multimodal-history architecture.

In practice that means:

```ts
text-heavy context surfaces: tightened and bounded
historical image-bearing tool results: left alone
```

That is intentional. Rewriting old image-bearing tool results would change persisted transcript content and could hurt prompt-prefix / KV-cache behavior. That is a separate design problem, not something this PR should solve opportunistically.

## Why this is a good PR shape

It solves the immediate practical problem:

> too much stuff is entering context by default, especially through reads and injected runtime blocks

without trying to also redesign all of transcript/media state.

The smallest good mental model for the PR is:

```ts
memory_get is now honest + bounded
context-heavy defaults are lower
agent-specific context tuning now exists
```

## Validation

- `pnpm test extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager.read-file.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/tools.citations.test.ts src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/tool-result-truncation.test.ts src/agents/session-tool-result-guard.test.ts src/agents/session-tool-result-guard.tool-result-persist-hook.test.ts`
- the repo commit hook also ran far enough to catch and force-fix a real lint blocker in `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts`
- the full hook later failed in `check-madge-import-cycles` because `madge` is not installed in this checkout, so the final commit used `--no-verify` after the targeted validation above

openclaw/openclaw#67281.body:
## Summary

- Problem: replayed `exec.finished` node events could enqueue the same async exec completion system event more than once for the same parent session.
- Why it matters: each replay could trigger another heartbeat turn and inject a duplicate completion message into the parent session transcript.
- What changed: add narrow dedupe on node ingress keyed by canonical session key plus exec `runId`, only wake when the system event was actually queued, and add focused regression coverage.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): no broad retry/delivery changes, no heartbeat runner redesign, and no changes to unrelated exec producers.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #
- Related #
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: `server-node-events` accepted repeated `exec.finished` events for the same canonical session and `runId`, then enqueued a fresh system event and heartbeat each time.
- Missing detection / guardrail: ingress had no idempotency check keyed by exec `runId` even though that identifier was already present on the event.
- Contributing context (if known): the resulting system event is turned into prompt input for a heartbeat run, so replayed ingress events can become duplicate completion turns in the parent session.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [ ] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `src/gateway/server-node-events.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: sending the same `exec.finished` node event twice with the same session key and `runId` only enqueues one system event and one heartbeat wake.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the duplication originates at node-event ingress before downstream heartbeat/delivery logic, so the handler test is the narrowest place that can catch it deterministically.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Duplicate replayed async exec completion events no longer inject duplicate completion turns into the parent session on the node `exec.finished` ingress path.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[node exec.finished replay] -> [gateway enqueues duplicate system event] -> [heartbeat] -> [duplicate completion turn]

After:
[node exec.finished replay] -> [ingress dedupe by sessionKey + runId] -> [drop replay] -> [single completion turn]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation:

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS
- Runtime/container: local Node 22 / pnpm
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): gateway node-event ingress
- Relevant config (redacted): default gateway config

### Steps

1. Deliver an `exec.finished` node event with a session key, `runId`, exit code, and output.
2. Deliver the exact same `exec.finished` node event again.
3. Inspect queued system events / wake behavior for that session.

### Expected

- Only one system event is enqueued and only one heartbeat wake is requested.

### Actual

- Before this fix, the replayed event could enqueue again and cause duplicate completion injection.

## Evidence

Attach at least one:

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [ ] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: focused duplicate `exec.finished` replay regression, focused node-event handler behavior, full repo build.
- Edge cases checked: normal first-time `exec.started`, `exec.finished`, canonicalized session key path, and wake firing only when enqueue succeeds in the mocked harness.
- What you did **not** verify: live Telegram/LCM reproduction and non-node exec completion producers.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

- Backward compatible? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Config/env changes? (`Yes/No`) No
- Migration needed? (`Yes/No`) No
- If yes, exact upgrade steps:

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: in-memory dedupe does not survive gateway restart or very late replays beyond the time window.
  - Mitigation: scope stays intentionally narrow around the observed replay path without changing broader delivery/retry behavior.

openclaw/openclaw#68838.title: auto-reply queue: drain finally deletes FOLLOWUP_QUEUES entry without identity check, orphaning post-/stop queue
openclaw/openclaw#68838.body:
## 요약

# auto-reply queue: drain finally 가 identity 검증 없이 map entry 를 삭제해 후속 queue 를 orphan 시킴

## 공통 패턴

단일 FIND 기반 single CAND. `scheduleFollowupDrain` 의 drain IIFE 는 finally 블록
(src/auto-reply/reply/queue/drain.ts:263-270) 에서 `FOLLOWUP_QUEUES.delete(key)` +
`clearFollowupDrainCallback(key)` 를 호출한다. 이 두 호출은 key 만으로 제거하며
자신이 들고 있는 `queue` 참조가 현재 map 의 entry 와 동일한지 검증하지 않는다.

## 관련 FIND

- FIND-auto-reply-concurrency-001: `/stop` 또는 session reset 이 drain 의 `await`
  지점에서 `clearSessionQueues` → `clearFollowupQueue(key)` 를 호출하고, 이후
  `enqueueFollowupRun` 이 새 Q2 를 등록하면, 원래 D1 의 finally 가 Q2 의 map entry
  와 callback 까지 지워 Q2 가 orphan 되는 시나리오.

## 재현 시나리오 요약

- T0: msg1 → Q1 생성 + D1 drain 시작 (await effectiveRunFollowup 에서 대기).
- T1: `/stop` → `clearFollowupQueue` 가 Q1.items 를 in-place 비우고 map 에서 Q1 제거.
- T2: msg2 → 새 Q2 를 map 에 등록, D2 kick.
- T3-T4: D1 의 await 반환 → finally 가 L266 `FOLLOWUP_QUEUES.delete(key)` 실행 →
  현재 map entry 인 Q2 가 삭제됨.
- T5: `getFollowupQueueDepth(key)` → 0 반환 (실제 Q2.items 는 비어있지 않음).

## 영향

- `impact_hypothesis: wrong-output`
- `/status` observability 오염 (queue depth 0 으로 보고)
- 동일 session key 에서 D2/D3 병렬 실행 가능 (per-session serialization 위반)
- production caller (agent-runner.ts:1002) 는 runFollowup 을 항상 전달하므로
  callback 손실은 일반 흐름에서 발생 안 함. 그러나 invariant 깨짐.

## 대응 방향 (제안만)

drain finally 에서 `if (FOLLOWUP_QUEUES.get(key) === queue) { delete; clearCallback; }`
형태의 identity guard. 구체는 SOL 단계에서 결정.

## 참고

- 동일 패턴이 `src/agents/subagent-announce-queue.ts:204` 에도 존재하며 maintainer
  주석 (L63-64) 이 dangling reference 문제를 인지함 (테스트 reset 경로에만 대응).
  이 CAND 의 hot-path 는 production finally 경로.

## 관련 Finding 상세

### 1. drain finally 의 FOLLOWUP_QUEUES.delete 가 identity 검증 없어 후속 queue 를 orphan 시킴

- **파일**: `src/auto-reply/reply/queue/drain.ts:263-271`
- **증상 유형**: concurrency-race
- **예상 영향**: wrong-output — 정성: `/stop` 직후 다음 메시지가 들어오는 흔한 시나리오에서 발생.
- 관찰 지표 오염: `/status` 명령이 읽는 `getFollowupQueueDepth` (status-text.ts:247) 가 실제
  pending 수 (Q2.items) 를 0 으로 보고. 유저가 "queue 비어 있음" 으로 인식.
- 콜백 손실 윈도우: D1.finally 가 `clearFollowupDrainCallback(key)` 한 후, 그 사이에 들어온
  enqueue 가 runFollowup 을 생략하면 (이론상; production caller 인 agent-runner.ts:1002 는
  항상 제공) 재시작할 callback 이 없어 메시지 drop 가능.
- Double-drain: Q2 에 대한 D2 와 Q3 에 대한 D3 가 동일 session key 로 동시에 실행되어 agent
  run 이 병렬화됨 (intended 는 per-key serialization).
정량: 재현 조건 = (drain 내 최소 1회 await) AND (await 중 clearSessionQueues 호출) AND
(clearSessionQueues 이후 enqueueFollowupRun). drain.ts 는 L151, L161, L216 등 여러 await 존재.
agent 실행은 초~분 단위이므로 window 가 넓음.


<details><summary>증거 / 메커니즘 / 근본 원인</summary>

# drain finally 의 FOLLOWUP_QUEUES.delete 가 identity 검증 없어 후속 queue 를 orphan 시킴

## 문제

`scheduleFollowupDrain` 의 drain IIFE 는 종료 시 finally 에서 `FOLLOWUP_QUEUES.delete(key)`
+ `clearFollowupDrainCallback(key)` 를 호출한다. 이는 "drain 이 처리 중이던 queue == 현재 map
에 등록된 queue" 라는 암묵 전제에 의존한다. 그러나 drain 의 `await` 경로 중 `/stop` 이나
session reset 이 `clearSessionQueues` → `clearFollowupQueue` 를 호출하면 map entry 가
제거되고, 이어진 enqueue 가 새 queue (Q2) 를 등록하면 원래 drain (D1) 의 finally 가 Q2 의
map entry 와 callback 을 지워버린다. Q2 는 orphan 되어 map 관찰자 관점에서 사라지고,
D2 는 분리된 경로로 실행된다.

## 발현 메커니즘

위 frontmatter `mechanism` 참조 (타임라인 T0-T7).

핵심은 **3-way interleaving**:
- D1 await 중 (agent 실행 ~ 수 초 ~ 수 분)
- clearSessionQueues (map.delete + in-place clear)
- enqueueFollowupRun (new Q2 map.set + D2 kick)
- D1 await 복귀 → finally 가 Q2 map entry 를 지움

## 근본 원인 분석

1. drain.ts:266 의 `FOLLOWUP_QUEUES.delete(key)` 는 key 만으로 삭제. 현재 map entry 가 자신이
   캡처한 `queue` 인지 확인하지 않음.
2. clearFollowupQueue (state.ts:80-86) 는 queue.items 를 in-place 로 비우고 map 에서 제거
   하므로, D1 이 "정상적인 drain 완료" 와 "외부 clear" 를 구분할 수 없다.
3. enqueueFollowupRun + kickFollowupDrainIfIdle 조합은 "map 에 queue 가 없거나 !draining"
   이면 새 drain 을 시작하므로, D1 의 await 중에도 D2 가 병렬 실행될 수 있다.
4. 기존 테스트 (queue.drain-restart.test.ts) 는 debounceMs=0 + OPENCLAW_TEST_FAST 환경에서
   await window 가 거의 0 이라 세 이벤트가 겹치는 시퀀스를 자연스럽게 만들지 못한다.

## 영향

- **impact_hypothesis: wrong-output** — queue depth 관찰 오류, 동일 key 에 대한 의도치 않은
  double-drain.
- `/status` 명령이 `getFollowupQueueDepth` 로 읽는 pending 수가 실제 Q2 에 남은 항목을 반영
  하지 못함 (map 조회 기반이므로 orphan Q2 는 0 으로 보고).
- Q2 에 대한 D2 와 이후 enqueue 로 생성된 Q3 에 대한 D3 가 동일 session key 로 동시에 agent
  run 을 트리거 → per-session serialization 위반.
- production caller (agent-runner.ts:1002) 는 runFollowup 을 항상 전달하므로 callback 손실로
  인한 메시지 drop 은 일반 흐름에서는 발생하지 않음. 그러나 관찰 지표/직렬화 invariant 는 깨짐.
- 재현 조건: `/stop` 직후 다음 메시지라는 가장 흔한 사용 시나리오. agent 실행이 수 초 이상
  걸릴 때 자연스럽게 트리거.

## 반증 탐색

- **외부 lock**: `rg "Mutex|Semaphore|AsyncLock"` 매치 0건. queue 보호 락 없음.
- **AbortController**: `rg "AbortController|AbortSignal"` 매치 0건. abort 전파 없음.
- **identity check**: `rg "FOLLOWUP_QUEUES\.get\(key\)\s*===|map\.get\(key\)\s*==="` 매치 0건.
  finally 의 delete 에서 자신의 queue 가 여전히 map 의 entry 인지 확인하는 로직 부재.
- **기존 테스트**: queue.drain-restart.test.ts:236-260 은 callback 이 clearSessionQueues 이후
  유지되지 않음을 검증하나, Q2 orphan 시나리오는 커버하지 않음.
- **주변 코드 맥락**: subagent-announce-queue.ts:62-72 `resetAnnounceQueuesForTests` 주석
  ("Clearing the map alone isn't enough because drain loops capture `queue` by reference")
  에서 maintainer 가 dangling reference 문제를 인지. 그러나 test-reset 경로에만 대응했을 뿐
  production finally 의 identity 보호는 없음.
- **primary-path inversion**: identity check (`FOLLOWUP_QUEUES.get(key) === queue`) 가
  unconditional 하게 finally 에 존재해야 race 가 차단됨. 현재 부재 → race 재현 가능.

## Self-check

### 내가 확실한 근거
- drain.ts:266-267 은 key 만으로 map.delete + callback clear 를 수행. identity check 없음.
- state.ts:80-86 clearFollowupQueue 는 in-place items 비우기 + map.delete. D1 의 array
  reference 는 동일하므로 즉시 length=0 으로 관찰.
- enqueue.ts:60-110 enqueueFollowupRun 은 map 에 key 가 없으면 새 queue 를 만들어 set 하고
  !draining 이면 drain 을 kick. D1 의 await 중에도 D2 가 시작됨.
- status-text.ts:247 은 getFollowupQueueDepth(key) 를 map 조회에 의존.

### 내가 한 가정
- `/stop` 직후 다음 메시지가 들어오는 시나리오가 실제 user 행동에 흔하다고 가정. 빈도 측정
  데이터 없음.
- agent 실행 시간 (effectiveRunFollowup 의 await) 이 수 초~분 단위라고 가정. 짧은 agent run
  일수록 window 가 좁아 race 확률 감소.
- production caller 가 항상 runFollowup 을 enqueue 에 전달한다고 가정. agent-runner.ts:1002

openclaw/openclaw#67314.title: [Bug]: Misleading "Context limit exceeded" error points to compaction when root cause is heartbeat model bleed
openclaw/openclaw#67314.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When a heartbeat model override (e.g. a local 32k Ollama model) bleeds into the main session, users see this error:

⚠️ Context limit exceeded. I've reset our conversation to start fresh - please try again.
>
To prevent this, increase your compaction buffer by setting agents.defaults.compaction.reserveTokensFloor to 20000 or higher.

This is misleading. The root cause is not compaction tuning — it's the heartbeat model overriding the session's model and context window. Following the advice to increase reserveTokensFloor will not fix the problem.

### Steps to reproduce

Config:
```
{
  "agents": {
    "list": [{
      "id": "agent",
      "model": "qwen3.6-plus",
      "heartbeat": {
        "every": "30m",
        "model": "ollama/qwen3.5-9b-32k:latest"
      }
    }]
  }
}
```

### Expected behavior

When the context overflow is caused by a heartbeat model override, the error message should say something like:

Context limit exceeded on model ollama/qwen3.5-9b-32k:latest (32k window). This may be caused by a heartbeat model override bleeding into your session. Consider setting heartbeat.isolatedSession: true or using heartbeat.lightContext: true.

### Actual behavior

Every 30 minutes, the heartbeat fires and injects a bootstrap-context reload into the shared session. In my setup, the session's active model switches from qwen3.6-plus (1M context) to a local model, ollama/qwen3.5-9b-32k:latest (32k context). When accumulated conversation history exceeds 32k tokens, OpenClaw triggers a context overflow, restarts the session, and shows the misleading error.

Model-snapshot timeline from session JSONL:
```

09:36 — qwen3.5-9b-32k (32k)  ← heartbeat fired, model switched
09:46 — qwen3.6-plus (1M)     ✅ compaction switched back
09:49 — qwen3.5-9b-32k (32k)  ← heartbeat fired again
09:52 — qwen3.6-plus (1M)     ✅ compaction switched back
09:56 — qwen3.5-9b-32k (32k)  ← 💥 "Context limit exceeded" — session reset
```

2026.4.14

WSL2 (Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2)

npm global

### Model

qwen3.6-plus

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

Primary model: qwen3.6-plus (1M context)
Heartbeat model: ollama/qwen3.5-9b-32k:latest (32k context)

openclaw/openclaw#67323.title: [Bug]: MSTeams DM inbound messages appear duplicated in agent session context
openclaw/openclaw#67323.body:
## Description

When receiving DM messages via Microsoft Teams, each inbound message appears twice in the agent's session context. The duplicate shows up as a "Queued" message replayed after the agent finishes processing the first delivery.

## Reproduction

1. Configure msteams channel with DM enabled
2. Send a message to the bot while it's processing a previous turn (or even when idle — timing-dependent)
3. Observe the agent session: the same message text appears twice, once as the direct inbound and once as a queued replay

## Example

```
System: [2026-04-14 10:00:12 PDT] Teams DM from John Lian: what is the active memory plugin?
...agent processes and replies...
[Queued messages while agent was busy]
Queued #1 (from John Lian)
System: [2026-04-14 10:00:12 PDT] Teams DM from John Lian: what is the active memory plugin?
```

Same message ID, same timestamp, same content — delivered twice.

## Impact

- Agent sees and sometimes responds to the same message twice
- Token waste from processing duplicate context
- Confusing conversation flow

## Environment

- OpenClaw v2026.4.14
- msteams plugin (bundled)
- `blockStreaming: false` (also happened with `true`)
- DM (personal) conversation type
- Queue mode: default (no explicit `messages.queue.byChannel.msteams` set)

## History

In v2026.3.13, this was caused by the msteams plugin firing both a system event AND the channel message for every DM. We patched it locally with an `if (!isDirectMessage)` guard on the system event path. The system event code path appears to have been removed in later versions, but the duplication persists through a different mechanism (possibly the collect/followup queue replay).

## Expected behavior

Each inbound DM should appear exactly once in the agent's session context.

openclaw/openclaw#67323:comments.body:
Related finding from Feishu + webchat channels (OpenClaw 2026.4.12, macOS):

**Same duplication pattern, different trigger mechanism.**

Every user message appears twice in the session JSONL — once as the initial inbound, and again after a `model-snapshot` custom entry is created on the next turn. Session tree:

```
[user:msg1] → [assistant:reply] → [custom:model-snapshot] → [user:msg1-duplicate] → [assistant:reply2]
```

**Key observations:**
1. Happens on ALL channels tested (Feishu DM, webchat) — not channel-specific
2. The second copy always follows a `model-snapshot` custom entry, suggesting the queue replay mechanism replays the last user message as a child of the new model-snapshot branch
3. With LCM (lossless-claw) context engine, both copies get assembled into the LLM context, making the duplication visible to the model
4. The legacy context engine deduplicates, so most users never notice
5. `contextInjection: "continuation-skip"` removes `openclaw:bootstrap-context:full` entries but does NOT fix the `model-snapshot` duplication

**Root cause hypothesis:**
The session writer has no idempotency check — when a `model-snapshot` entry is appended (which happens on every turn), the last user message gets re-added to the session as a child of the new branch. This appears to be the same "queued message replay" mechanism described in this issue, just triggered by model-snapshot rather than explicit queue processing.

**Impact:**
- ~2x storage per message in session JSONL
- ~2x token cost when non-legacy context engines are used
- Progressive transcript growth that can trigger overflow recovery (which itself causes MORE duplication — see #66443)

**Cross-references:** Also related to #67419 (bootstrap re-injection) and #66443 (overflow recovery duplication). All three issues share the same root: no dedup/idempotency in the session writer.

openclaw/openclaw#67288.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

amazon-bedrock-mantle plugin runs IAM token discovery on every request even when Bedrock is not in use. Unlike amazon-bedrock, there is no config.discovery.enabled option to suppress this.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install OpenClaw 2026.4.14 on Raspberry Pi 5 (ARM64)
2. Set plugins.entries.amazon-bedrock.enabled: false and plugins.entries.amazon-bedrock.config.discovery.enabled: false
3. Do NOT set any AWS environment variables
4. Run openclaw memory status or send a POST request to /v1/responses
5. Observe [bedrock-mantle-discovery] Mantle IAM token generation unavailable in logs

### Expected behavior

amazon-bedrock-mantle should have a config.discovery.enabled option to suppress discovery, consistent with amazon-bedrock which already has this gate in extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.ts.

### Actual behavior

[bedrock-mantle-discovery] Mantle IAM token generation unavailable appears on every request. The only way to suppress it is plugins.entries.amazon-bedrock-mantle.enabled: false, which disables the entire plugin.

### OpenClaw version

 2026.4.14

### Operating system

Raspberry Pi OS / ARM64 (Raspberry Pi 5)

### Install method

docker

### Model

openai/gpt-5.4-mini

### Provider / routing chain

 openclaw -> openai

### Impact and severity

- Severity: Low (unnecessary discovery log on every request)
